1 · Read the explanation.
Proposing, objecting, supporting

Proposing with an infinitive. The frames built on would be are completed by to + verb: One alternative would be to install…, A better way forward would be to fit…, The simplest option would be to move it. These are the most formal of the set and the most common in writing.

Proposing with -ing. Worth is always followed by -ing: Would it be worth putting in fake cameras? So are the frames with the preposition in: any point in changing…, no harm in trying…. And suggest keeps its pattern from lesson 33: I would suggest fitting….

Proposing with a clause. What if we paint the walls? treats the idea as a real possibility; What if we painted the walls? is one step more tentative, and is the safer form in a meeting where you are not in charge. How about and What about take -ing: How about painting the walls?

Objecting. English objects with a reason attached: I do not think that is an option, because…, I am not convinced by those, We need to take cost into consideration. A bare no ends a discussion that the speaker usually wants to continue.

Supporting and deciding. That would be an effective solution, There is no harm in doing that as well, Let us do that; I will look into it. A proposal without somebody named to act on it is a conversation, not a decision.

The commonest errors at this level
  • Would it be worth to put in cameras?
  • Is there any point to change the lock?
  • There is no harm to try it.
  • One alternative would be installing cameras — possible, but the infinitive is standard here.
  • What if we to paint the walls? or What about paint the walls?

Two things to watch

1 — Worth, point in, harm in all take -ing. Three phrases, one rule, and they account for most of the mistakes in this stage.

2 — Reject with a reason, always. I do not think that is an option, I am afraid followed by the cost, the effort or the evidence. Without the reason it sounds like a refusal to discuss.

5 · Worked example. Read it before you do the exercises.
Turning an idea into three different proposals

The idea: fit movement-sensor lights in the yard.

Version 1 — the formal frame. A better way forward would be is completed by an infinitive: A better way forward would be to fit movement-sensor lights.

Version 2 — testing the water. Worth demands -ing: Would it be worth fitting movement-sensor lights? This invites an objection instead of asking for agreement.

Version 3 — the most tentative. What if takes a clause, and the past tense makes it softer: What if we fitted a couple and reviewed it in a month?

And the objection. Whatever you propose, expect: We need to take cost into consideration. That frame ends with a noun, so name the thing: cost, time, the neighbours, the winter.

13 · Read this before the extra practice.
Fixed frames, and the form each one takes

These phrases are frames: the words do not change, and the form after them does not change either.

Followed by to + verb: One alternative would be to install cameras · A better way forward would be to fit sensor lights · The simplest option would be to move it · We need to take cost into consideration.

Followed by -ing: Would it be worth putting in fake ones? · Is there any point in changing the lock? · There is no harm in trying it for a month · I would suggest fitting two of them · How about painting the walls?

Followed by a clause: What if we painted the walls? — and note that what if takes either the present (a real plan) or the past (a more tentative one), never what if we to paint.

Objecting without stopping the meeting

I do not think that is an option and I am not convinced by those are complete objections, but on their own they leave the group with nothing. Each has to be followed by a reason, and in a working meeting, ideally by an alternative — which is what the proposing frames are for. We need to take cost into consideration is the softest objection of the set, because it names a factor rather than rejecting a person’s idea.

Supporting is short: That would be an effective solution. Deciding is shorter still, and needs a name attached: Let us do that. I will look into it. A discussion that ends without somebody saying I will has not decided anything.

Register: How about…? and What if…? are spoken; One alternative would be… and A better way forward would be… belong in a written proposal or a formal meeting. Both sets say the same thing; choosing the wrong one is not a grammar mistake but it is noticed.

Errors to watch: Would it be worth to put → worth putting · Is there any point to change → any point in changing · There is no harm to try → no harm in trying · How about to paint → How about painting · One alternative would be installing in this frame → would be to install · take into consideration the cost is possible but heavy → take cost into consideration.

1 · Read the model article.
Model · an advice article in four paragraphs

What to do about vandalism at a small site

Start with a definition, because vandalism and theft need different answers. If nothing has been taken, you are dealing with damage for its own sake, usually late at night, usually in the one corner nobody can see from the road. Before proposing anything, analyse the pattern: two incidents this month, both after eleven, both in the unlit corner, and the gate lock untouched, which tells you access was over the wall.

The obvious answer is a security camera, and for most small sites it is the wrong one. Cameras are expensive to install, difficult to maintain, and incapable of stopping anything by themselves; somebody still has to watch the recording and act on it. Fake cameras are cheaper and not quite useless, but anybody who has looked at one twice is not convinced. A better way forward would be to fit movement-sensor lights: a well-lit corner is a poor place to spend twenty minutes with a spray can, and two of your own staff are probably capable of fitting them in an afternoon.

There is no harm in adding one cheap precaution as well — anti-climb paint on the wall they came over, for instance. Is there any point in changing a lock that was never broken? None, and money spent there is money not spent on the lights.

The mistake most people make is treating this as a purchase rather than an experiment. Fix a review date, write down what you expect to happen, and be precise about what you are measuring. If the incidents stop, you have your answer. If they move to another corner, you have learned something worth more than the lights cost.
